podcast.body: The title of this iconic song originated from an act of vandalism by Kathleen Hanna, a friend of Kurt Cobain and member of Bikini Kill. During a night of drinking in the winter of 1990, Hanna spray-painted "Kurt smells like teen spirit" on Cobain's bedroom wall in Olympia, Washington, referencing a trendy girls' deodorant used by Toby Vail (another Bikini Kill member whom Kurt liked). Kurt, who didn't wear deodorant, misinterpreted this as a compliment about embodying teenage rebellion, only learning the true, less profound inspiration after the song's writing, recording, and release. "It wasn't until after the song was written, recorded, and released that Kurt found out what had actually inspired one of the greatest rock and roll songs of all time."

podcast.title: Rehearsal Demo
podcast.body: An early, raw rehearsal demo of this song from late 1990 or early 1991 was included in the *With the Lights Out* box set. This demo, which Kurt Cobain called "Smells Like Teen Spirit," featured their new drummer Dave Grohl and differed significantly from the final *Nevermind* version, being "almost a minute longer" with different words and arrangements. "It's a rehearsal demo of a new song that Kurt called Smells Like Teen Spirit. And it's one of the first things that featured their new drummer Dave Grohl."

podcast.body: An advanced single for "Nevermind" was sent to radio stations on August 27, 1991, intended merely to "excite the freaks" at alternative stations, not as the primary single. Despite low expectations for the album (initially hoping for 100,000 sales), when this song hit the radio, listeners reacted "ballistic," leading to the single selling out everywhere upon its release on September 10th. "When that first song hit the radio, Listers went ballistic."

podcast.body: Kurt Cobain aimed to write a song in the style of the Pixies, characterized by loud/soft/loud/soft dynamics, later admitting it was an attempt to "rip off" the Pixies. It began much faster and more punk rock, with Kurt providing the riff and chorus. Chris Novoselic suggested slowing the verses, and Dave Grohl changed the drum beat, leading to the song's distinctive structure. "Kurt was looking to write a song in the style of the Pixies, which made a lot of loud, soft, loud, soft dynamics."

podcast.body: Released to radio on August 27, 1991, this song was Track One on the "Nevermind" album and was initially intended as a "throw away" single to "soften people up" for what the band believed would be the album's main hit, Track Three. However, it unexpectedly became a massive success and a defining anthem of the grunge movement. "It was decided that Track One would be the first single, song that would kind of soften people up for what was going to be the real hit from the album, which was Track Three. However, it didn't quite work out as planned. That throw away for single ended up, well you know."

podcast.body: The CD single for "Smells Like Teen Spirit" was released on August 27, 1991, the same day as Pearl Jam's *Ten* album. Iver Hamilton from Polygram Records brought the CD single to a radio station, where it was first played at 11:38 AM, potentially marking its Canadian debut. The song generated an immediate and overwhelming listener response, leading to repeated airplay throughout the day due to high demand on request lines. It was also played at The Kingdom (also known as Energy) in Burlington, Ontario, on a Thursday night for an alternative dance event, where attendees already knew all the lyrics, demonstrating its stunning immediate impact. "I put it on and smells like teen spirit starts."

podcast.body: The CD single was released on August 27, 1991, the same day as Pearl Jam's *Ten*. The speaker, working at a radio station, was given the single by Iver Hamilton from Polygram Records and played it at 11:38 AM, believing it was the first time the song was played in Canada. The phone lines immediately melted down with requests, leading to repeated plays throughout the day. A promotional copy was played at an alternative dance night at The Kingdom in Burlington just two days later, on a Thursday, where attendees already knew all the lyrics, demonstrating its immediate and stunning impact. The song's lyrics became widely known, similar to "Satisfaction." "I think I'm the first person in Canada to play the song. I think put it on and the phone immediately started to ring."

podcast.body: The anthemic and irresistible lead single from "Nevermind," written by Kurt Cobain as a Pixies homage and named after a deodorant brand. Its "anarchistic, thrashy high school pep rally" video gained MTV power rotation. It debuted on the Hot 100 in late November 1991, driven by strong single sales (7th in sales vs. 73rd in airplay by mid-December), and peaked at number one on the Modern Rock chart for one week in late November '91. "Smells like teen spirit, the song Cobain wrote as a pixie's homage and named after a brand of deodorant aimed at teenagers was both anthemic and irresistible."

podcast.body: This 1991 video is credited with ushering in the Grunge era. It was shot on August 17, 1991, at GMT Studios in Culver City, California, directed by Sam Bayer. The video featured real-life fans who actively destroyed the set, creating an explosive atmosphere filled with smoke and chalk dust, which made breathing difficult. The total cost was approximately $50,000. Kurt Cobain's guitar used in the video was later sold at auction in 2022 for 3.5 million pounds. "And who could forget the video that ushered in the whole Grunge era in 1991?"

podcast.body: This CD single, released on August 27, 1991, was initially seen by its record label as a "tough sell" due to Nirvana's vocal punk rock stance and the song's heavy sound, contrasting with the prevailing hair metal and keyboard-based alt-rock of the time. Despite low expectations from the label, it became a "monster" hit, reaching the top 10 in 21 countries and number 1 in 4, ushering in the age of grunge and sparking a massive punk rock comeback. "It was a monster that did well everywhere, including on the top 40 charts where it reached the top 10 in 21 countries and all the way to number 1 in 4."

podcast.body: This track was a massive hit on the radio around the time Radiohead's "Drill" EP was being produced. Radiohead's managers, "enamored" with its success, attempted to make the EP sound like it, resulting in a "confused mess." It is also considered one of the three great "slacker anthems" of the early 90s, alongside Radiohead's "Creep" and Beck's "Loser." podcast.body: Three takes of "Smells Like Teen Spirit" were recorded in the studio, with the final version being essentially the middle take (take two of three). More takes might have been done, but Kurt Cobain's voice was "shot from all the yelling and screaming." The single was released on September 10th, 1991. "So what we hear is essentially the middle one take two of three."
